name: Gestational Trophoblastic Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: FIGO Diagnostic Criteria for Gestational Trophoblastic Neoplasia

criteria.description: Persistently elevated or rising serum beta-hCG levels beyond expected post-pregnancy decline
Ultrasound evidence of characteristic molar pattern (snowstorm or cluster of grapes appearance)
Histopathological confirmation of trophoblastic proliferation or molar tissue
Clinical features such as abnormal uterine bleeding or uterine enlargement disproportionate to gestational age

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of persistently elevated beta-hCG plus either characteristic ultrasound findings or histopathological confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires correlation of clinical, laboratory, imaging, and pathological findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Markedly elevated serum beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (beta-hCG)
searchTerms: very high beta-hCG levels in blood

pathognomonic.symptomName: Ultrasound appearance of hydropic villi with 'snowstorm' pattern

common.symptomName: Uterine enlargement greater than expected for gestational age
searchTerms: uterus larger than expected for pregnancy stage
excessive nausea and vomiting in pregnancy
ovarian cysts due to hormone changes
anemia caused by heavy uterine bleeding
blood loss anemia due to uterine bleeding

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory symptoms due to pulmonary metastases
searchTerms: respiratory symptoms due to lung spread
brain lesions causing weakness or numbness

laboratory: Thyroid function abnormalities in some cases
imaging: Pelvic ultrasound showing 'snowstorm' or 'cluster of grapes' appearance
Chest X-ray or CT scan showing pulmonary metastases
MRI brain for cerebral metastases if neurological symptoms present
genetic: Complete hydatidiform mole: diploid androgenetic origin (paternal genome only)
Partial mole: triploid karyotype with two paternal and one maternal set

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of intrauterine pregnancy on ultrasound
Lower beta-hCG levels relative to gestational age
Pain localized to one side with adnexal tenderness
Presence of retained products of conception on ultrasound
History of vaginal bleeding and cramping
Malignant trophoblastic tumor with rapid metastasis

redFlags: Rapidly rising or plateaued beta-hCG after evacuation
Signs of metastatic disease (e.g., hemoptysis, neurological symptoms)
Severe uterine bleeding or signs of uterine rupture
references: FIGO Oncology Committee. FIGO staging for gestational trophoblastic neoplasia 2018.
Seckl MJ, Sebire NJ, Berkowitz RS. Gestational trophoblastic disease: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up. Ann Oncol. 2013.
Orphanet: Gestational trophoblastic disease. Orphanet Report Series, 2021.
